sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The verb form usually shows who is doing the action, so Hungarian often leaves the subject pronoun unstated.

Írok already means 'I write' — tacking Én in front (Én írok) isn't wrong, but it's like saying 'I, I write'; the ending has already told you who. A named subject like Anna, though, has to be stated — the verb form alone can't tell you it's her and not you.
